title: ~[]byte generic functions cannot accept a bare nil literal
claim: TaintBytes, IsTaintedBytes, and VisitBytes are generic over T ~[]byte; Go cannot infer T from an untyped nil literal alone, so taint.IsTaintedBytes(nil) (and the equivalent VisitBytes/TaintBytes calls) fails to compile with 'cannot infer T', even though a typed nil ([]byte(nil) or a nil []byte variable) works correctly.

title: Undocumented drop condition: invalid Origin values are silently rejected
claim: TaintString/TaintBytes doc comments list the drop conditions but omit that an invalid/unnamed Origin value (zero or above OriginCount) is also silently rejected via internal/taint/request/table.go's validOrigin, even though Source.Origin is a plain exported field an external caller can set to any uint8.

title: go doc on the public package hides Origin/VulnerabilityType methods
claim: Origin and VulnerabilityType are type aliases to internal/model/constants types; go doc resolves methods by declaring package, so go doc -all ./taint shows no String()/JSON methods for these aliases even though they exist and work, leaving external readers of the taint package's own docs unable to discover them.

title: Public API has no production caller; only its own unit tests exercise it
claim: All current sources/sinks call internal/taint/request's Analysis/IsTainted*/Visit* directly, not taint.TaintString/TaintBytes/IsTainted*/Visit*. A repo-wide search for the import path finds only taint/taint_test.go and the never-invoked tooling import in orchestrion.tool.go, so this public surface's correctness is validated only by its own test file.
